content.title: About
content.content: Cereal with peanut butter is a ready‑to‑eat breakfast consisting of whole grain flakes sweetened and coated with a smooth peanut butter spread. The product combines crunchy cereal with a rich nutty flavor, providing a quick source of energy and nutrients.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Peanut butter has been used in breakfast cereals for over 30 years.
The flakes are often fortified with B‑vitamins and iron.
The grain‑nut combination improves the bioavailability of certain minerals.
The product is packaged in convenient single‑serve bags for easy transport and storage.
In many countries similar cereals are sold under different brand names but with comparable formulations.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Whole grain flakes provide slowly digestible carbs that sustain energy levels for several hours.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: Peanut butter adds about 8 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle repair and growth.

items.title: Contains healthy fats
items.content: Monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fatty acids from peanut butter promote heart health.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: Fortified cereals often include iron, zinc, vitamin B6 and folate, essential for metabolism.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Whole grains supply fiber that aids normal digestion.

items.title: Peanut allergy
items.content: The product can trigger severe allergic reactions in individuals sensitive to peanuts.

items.title: Added sugar
items.content: Some varieties contain added sugars, which may contribute to weight gain if consumed in excess.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: The combination of cereal and butter makes the product energy‑dense; portion control is advised.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Salt is often added for flavor, which may be unsuitable for people monitoring sodium intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cereal with peanut butter can be enjoyed dry, with milk or a plant‑based beverage, or mixed into yogurt, fruit, and nuts for a more filling breakfast.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the package in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, reseal the bag tightly to prevent moisture absorption and preserve crunchiness.
